author: Rokit
subject: Re: Raid Mobs
content_md:
There is a lot of rhetoric that will dogpile you for wanting trash to be made reasonable.

Tempest Keep is a great example of restrained raid trash. The pulls are puzzles (like BWL trash), and there are 1-4 of them between bosses. Molten Core, Temple of Ahn'Qiraj and Naxxramas have some pretty repetitive, excessive, and uninteresting trash. Especially in particularly infamous stretches (After Twin Emps, After Razuvious, etc).

Cleaning up trash in MC first would be a boon for the lower access raiders. I think there are a few cheap and easy steps to get there, with MC in mind.

- Remove trash that is not an encounter in and of itself (non-gatekeeping random Giants, random imp packs that are not near a boss)
- Identify 2-4 trash pulls that are nearest to each boss and link their pull / respawn behavior (a DB edit, "easy" and troubleshootable)
- Fold trash loot into boss loot tables as its own additional drop; increasing the items dropped by each boss (excluding Rag) by one.
There are a LOT of repercussions to doctoring the trash in vanilla. I would label them "Growing Pains" but others would call them "Unfaithful" or that it would punish people who had not yet gotten the opportunity to farm Naxx trash etc. Any changes to existing blizzard content will always earn some pushback.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Raid Mobs
content_md:
I think this is a great topic for discussion. I don't agree that trash should be removed entirely, but TWoW devs certainly have a bit of an unhealthy obsession with trash in raid instances. Both ES and LKH were at release filled to the brim with trash. While ES was mercifully toned down a bit, for LKH I don't think *anyone* was unhappy when Moroes died in the Opera audience for a few weeks, yet he was moved back to the stage adding another ~7 trash packs to a full clear. And the forced clearing of all the imps in side-rooms is one of the most disliked parts of LKH.

> **Balake wrote: Tue May 16, 2023 7:28 pm**
> Each type of trash pack should have atmost 3-4 spawns in a raid, the lab packs in Patchwerk room for example serve no purpose other than to slow the raid down. Once you kill 3-4 of them, you pretty much prove you can do them and shouldn't need to do any further (in that lockout).

I think this is a great way of conceptualizing the problem. What does the 6th identical trash pack add to a raid? Outside of very specific circumstances (like the Anubisaths between Huhuran and Twin Emps where untangling their patrols *is* the encounter challenge, annoying as it may be) - pretty much nothing.

 **1) Trash should not respawn.**
Outside of gauntlets like Suppression Room, pre-Fankriss, abom wing slimes, pre-Loatheb - what's the point of having trash respawn? A veteran guild will never run into respawn issues and if you're progressing and learning encounters it's just a massive annoyance having to re-clear trash after 2 hours. You've shown you can beat the pack, why should an unfortunate wipe or even just a person joining late set you back to having to redo the entire thing? - Sidenote: Custom content like LKH already does this.

 **2) Trash should not be designed or evaluated with skips in mind.**
You know what's *not* in my hero/character fantasy? Pressing myself against a wall in a toxic slime trench in Naxxramas, trying to sneak around like a bandit, blowing Invis Pots to avoid the main mechanic of the game (combat). If trash is meant to be fought, the fight should be forced. If trash is not meant to be fought - why even include it? - Even Blizzard had its moments, there is zero trash between Heigan and Loatheb, Gluth and Thaddius. It's clearly not something that is "needed" for a proper Blizz-like raid.

 **3) Trash should not be too repetitive.**
I don't want trash removed, not at all. But you can weed out some identical packs without losing anything. Lab packs in BWL are kind of elegant - you get a small one as an introduction, then 4 mid-sized ones, before 2 final full-sized ones. That progression should be kept, But you can take out 2 of the mid-size packs and nobody will miss them (maybe bump sand droprate just a bit in return to help fresh raids build a stockpile).

> **Gantulga wrote: Wed May 17, 2023 12:39 am**
> The raid with a balanced trash/boss ratio and a model to be followed is AQ20.

I respectfully disagree. AQ20 has a lot of repetition. Bug packs before first boss, Anubisaths before Ossirian, bug packs before Ayamiss. You do the exact same fight 6+ times. And it would be a lot worse if people weren't skipping a massive stretch of trash by swimming through the water. AQ20 has some good design to it. But trash I feel is not one of its strengths.

Competitive speed clearing of raids originated after original vanilla. As original vanilla naxx got cleared by less than 1% of the entire playerbase. You can look up the  Kronos server for example, which had a big part in the entire scene developing itself as early as 2010. Feenix also had some of it and ofc Nostalrius and all the other 1.12.1 true servers that popped up like ED and whatnot.

author: Susannnnn
subject: Asking GM to help me punish the cheater
content_md:
On the morning of April 1st (Beijing time), I engaged in weapon trading on the World channel, and a player with ID jakewang requested me to send him an email using cash on delivery method. Subsequently, I fulfilled his request. However, when I went to retrieve the email, I inadvertently overlooked that he had sent me a payment email instead. Consequently, I unintentionally accepted the email and as a result, he deceived me by taking away 30 gold coins. Immediately after this incident occurred, I contacted GM for assistance. The GM requested evidence from me; however, due to the disappearance of the email upon retrieval, it was impossible for me to provide any proof. Therefore, I sincerely hope that GM can examine my email records despite their initial inability to do so. Nevertheless, they assured me that they would monitor the subsequent actions of this player.
In the afternoon when I logged into my account again, it came to my attention that this player had once again sent me another paid email with intentions of deceiving me for a second time. Such behavior is highly unethical and unacceptable. Although losing 30 gold coins does not significantly impact my gameplay experience personally; however,I am concerned about new players who may fall victim to such scams without knowing how to handle them appropriately. Henceforth,I implore GMs to take severe disciplinary action against these types of players in order to maintain a purified gaming environment and create a better world for all players!

下午我登录账号发现这位玩家又给我发送了一封付费邮件，还想骗我第二次，这种行为实在太恶劣了，我并不缺这30个金币，但是我想到还有很多新手玩家遇到这种情况被骗了怎么办呢？所以我请求GM一定要严厉处罚这种玩家，净化游戏环境，让我们的世界变得更美好！！！

subject: Thaddius loot table
content_md:
This is silly I know (RNG is weird sometimes, I get it), but has anyone else noticed the Thaddius loot table for T3 head tokens being unbalanced? According to the database, each token has a 33% chance to drop twice per kill. My guild has been killing Thaddius every week since late January (15 kills according to our raid log history) and we haven't seen the Pally, Hunter, Shaman, Druid token drop yet. Every week it's 2 of the other ones.

I get RNG is weird sometimes, but a 33% chance for something to drop 30 times (15 kills x 2 drops a week) has such a strong possibility to happen that it's basically statistically impossible for it not to. If you do the actual math, the odds of it dropping in 30 chances is 0.9999999999999997465%.

Anyway, just wondered if anyone else has experienced this or if a GM is just messing with us   wary_turtle_head

You suggest that re-adding world buffs to Tel'Abim would incentivize world PVP but do you really want to enjoy the world 'PVP' of the world buff meta? I can probably sum up the average 'PVP' encounter in the world buff meta that will occur 99% of the time
 - Shaman/Priest resses at a world buff location e.g. Songflower, ZG island and starts purging/dispelling people's buffs.
 - Gets killed by a raid/party
 - Waits whilst dead until the next group

I don't really think that's an enjoyable PVP experience and one that Tel'Abim should aim towards cultivating.

Outside of that, you have a host of other issues such as further unbalance in the raiding scene (as some classes benefit more from world buffs than others) and trivialising PvE content by making boss fights much shorter and mechanics less important.

What you 'enjoy' is cowardly griefing and toxicity.  It is not 'World PvP' as you put it.  Sitting there with a lowbie Shaman alt (or even worse, multiboxers who do this) and mass-purging world buffs from raiders is only going to create friction and make people want to raid (and PvP) far less often.

If all you believe in is indulging in epicaricacy, there are entire genres of PvP-focused games catering to that, MOBAs being one of them and shooter games (both FPS and TPS) being another.  There's also an Action RPG that is custom built from the ground up to cater to PvP players.  You get all the leveling and RPG mechanics along with full loot PvP and more in a game with a 'WoW-style' cartoony aesthetic that runs cross-platform and on mobile.

It isn't 'fun' to most people to have their world buffs purged by some clown sitting in a corner somewhere griefing level 60 raiders trying to get into a raid.  What that'll do is result in a Warlock & 3 people just summoning the rest of the raid inside and the worst you will be able to do is upset maybe 2 or 3 people at most before you die and start the cycle again.

Priest world PvP is actually mind-controlling characters and either attacking their buddies with the MC'd character or throwing them off a cliff and/or into lava.  While that is still trolling, the level of amusement for both enemy and victim is too funny to really be mad about it ;)
There's a clear difference there, but it is still something guilds will want to avoid so they'll send druids/rogues to scout around if the area is clear before they zerg in.  Just time-wasting nonsense.

This kind of nonsense is why 'World PvP' is a joke and always has been.  Tel'Abim died because of garbage like this ruining the few raid groups that wanted to form up.  Most newbies and lowbies who joined up just got ganked relentlessly by cowardly griefer 60s in the starter zones trying to 'farm' anyone who had War Mode on as well as anyone crossing over from uncontested to contested territory.

author: Akalix
subject: Re: GDPK, EPGP, HR...
content_md:
Concerning why GDKP is banned—it has been heavily directly linked to an increase in RMT/gold buying wherever permitted.

In order to maintain the integrity of our server’s economies, and ensure fair play, we opted to ban GDKP outright rather than fight the losing battle of preventing RMT in a setting where the idea of earned progression is replaced by “affording” progression.

Players are free to use whatever loot system they wish, so long as progression isn’t being sold.

I believe this problem comes from raiding with pugs. Player join one pug raid, kill single boss and get locked to that raid instance. I think it is totally reasonable consequence of raiding with pugs. Join some guild with raid schedule and you will be fine.

New formula has been introduced to exact an average which is more accurate than before.
 - Weekly Top Classes will be split in a larger sheet based on Class + Spec to introduce better representation.

Hello everyone,

Since Class Changes 2.0 it has become really hard to keep up with what's good and what's not for damage in raiding scene. For that purpose I have created a Sheet which will provide results as an info graph on Patchwerk style single target dps, as a showcase of "what's possible".

The purpose of this sheet is not to give a definitive result, nor is it there to exact an average result this early into the Class Changes 2.0. It is here to give you the top DPS performance on Patchwerk with the sole purpose of showcase.

The sheet will be updated weekly with:
 - Top Class, Spec & Style. (for the entire quarter)
 - Top Players For Class Damage-Wise. (weekly)
 - Weekly Top Damage numbers & guilds.
 - All results include log links.

You can find the sheet here:
[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ ... 2018728657](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GaKCpUEVT7s6JrCM8Ecap7B2ziMxe9dUSh_WYFzTTD4/edit?gid=2018728657#gid=2018728657)

![Image](https://imgur.com/a/KL0gQOq)

Disclaimers:
 - The following results are being collected as best overall since the official release of CC2 on a weekly basis - 1st of Nov 2024
 - The sheet & its future weekly updates do not account for unexpected Bugs/Buffs/Nerfs or any inadequacies that may have occurred that week.
 - Data is being collected exclusively from Turtlogs.com as it supports our custom content & will support future raids.
 - She sheet is updated daily & results will not be final until the weekly reset day.

Enjoy.

author: Maximan
subject: Emerald Sanctum Hard Mode Advice
content_md:
Is anyone able to help me with some general advice for ES hard mode? I run it for my guild and some weeks it goes fine, others it seems impossible. I can't figure out what we're doing wrong on the off weeks. People I ask all give me conflicting information. You can dispel 1 of Erenius' sleeps safely. You can't dispel anything. Erenius uses LoS. LoS doesn't matter, only range.

Last time I was 80 yards away from Erenius and still got put to sleep while healing the healers on Erenius' tank. I've been told that I was probably too close to Solinus and that he probably slept me, while also being told he can't sleep!

At the moment the way I plan it is this:

 1 tank on Erenius - 3 healers on that tank at max range - 1 healer on those healers at max range

Everyone on else on Solinus same as normal mode.

Our tank and healers have good enough gear that threat or healing isn't a problem. But even when the tank is the only person within 40 yards of Erenius, he's still getting put to sleep, which eventually means he loses threat to a healer in the Solinus group and Erenius goes wandering off. So there is obviously something I'm not aware of that's preventing us doing this successfully and I'd be very appreciative if anyone could advise :)

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Emerald Sanctum Hard Mode Advice
content_md:
Here is how our guild does it.

Positioning:
> B= boss
>  T= Tank
>  H= Heal
>  M = Melee
>  R = Ranged
>
>  B T< - 40 yards- > 3H <- 10 yards -> H&R <- 20 yards-> M B T

We put the addtank & healers into a separate grp. That makes it easy for them to heal the tank and one another (preferably always a druid, priest and shaman healer + a warrior tank for dealing with erennius)
Line of sight used to matter but i think it got patched, we stopped losing since it didnt seem to help us consistently and people kept getting slept eitherway. We found everyone but the addtank being in the main raids healers range helped more in peventing sleep deaths than trying to be cute with los.

There are some debuffs that are conditionally worth removing. The manadrain curses can be removed from tree druids. And the sleep the adds cast can be removed without issue. But due to the risk generally associated with dispelling. My advice as raidleader is, drop tremor totem and dont dispell anything. If the wrong stuff gets dispelled its much more devastating.

Make sure the melees stand at max melee range fanned out in the back half of the boss. He has a nasty aoe that he casts on random players in melee. It deals way too much damage if your melees clump.

Keep detect magic on the boss and ask a offensive shaman or piest to purge the buff that looks like the goblin shrink ray debuff (a blue bolt facing bottom left)

In the addphase let a pally pick up welps and ignore them. Burn down the elite adds. Focus spellcasters and leave scalebane for last.
Only bomb adds once all 3 elites are down.

Keep 2 tanks on the main boss that race for theeat until he transforms. The tank that gets booted off tried to climb up back into second place, but thats only needed i the MT eats too many breaths in p3 and shouldnt be an issue unless your grps dps is atroceous

With that we have little problems consistently killing him

author: Moongirl
subject: How do you Raid?
content_md:
**Greetings! I hope you are having a nice day!**  smiling_turtle_head

I've always been more of a solo player in WoW, and I have reached 60 on some classes. However, raiding always seemed like 'the thing to do' once you are max level. As a solo player, the process seems very complex and *I have no idea where to start*. I don't know if I want to get to Naxxaramas or Kharazan level, I just would like to experience a 'simple' Molten Core or Onyxia.

 1. Gear
How do you know when you are ready for a raid? I see the questline for the Tier 0.5 and it seems very difficult. But, if you are a healer or tank, do you even need to do it? Turtle has added a lot of new items and I don't know a clear indication for when you have the correct gear. I'm assuming each raid is different and would require certain stats, like specific resistances.

 2. Guild
I think most people do raids in a guild, which is understandable. However, most of these guilds need active people, or need you to join Discord. I usually take long breaks from WoW and I don't have discord, so you can see the difficulty. For an old game like WoW, I'm really confused why you can't just use in-game chat. My best chance is probably a pick-up group for raids, but what about the 'attunement'? (I think its called that?) For Molten Core, you need this douse, and for Emerald Sanctum you need to do Dire Maul East... but these don't appear easy for a solo player to do. To make this part short, is it too difficult to try and do Raid related things *without* a guild?

I would rather not make this post too long, but perhaps you can see my worries and confusion. I may not have the mindset for something like a raid in Turtle WoW, but it is a big achievement in Azeroth and I want to experience it, even just once. Besides, I do not know what else to do at max level other than RP and PvP, and I can only do leveling process so many times.

Thank you for taking the time to read this. Any tips will be appreciated. Have a great day, and good luck on your journey.   smiling_turtle_head

author: Bayanni
subject: Re: How do you Raid?
content_md:
For getting into raiding, the gear you need for MC and onward very much depends on your class. Healers generally can get away with less gear than a DPS and a DPS can get away with less than a tank.

It's unlikely you'd be able to join a raid team as a tank with pre-raid gear at this point in the server's life, there's too many geared people who can do better threat. A DPS will largely depend on what's available for them pre-raid, but for melees and hunters I typically see hit cap as the requirement. Zero idea on typical caster requirements but no green gear and all blues at least lvl 50 should get you to MC without a lot of hassle, it's not a hard raid by any stretch. Healers can get away with greens if they have a lot of +healing on it but otherwise just stack good blues from instances and quests and you're solid.

Attunements will require you to group with people, but this is usually done in world chat. MC requires BRD but can be done with a lava run easily enough. ES requires ST at some point and a few elites, but Azshara ones aren't too hard and the Hyjal one won't take long to find a group. BWL is just an UBRS run and those pop up fairly often. Onyxia, though, is not easy and would likely require you to just find 3-4 other people on the same part of the quest as you so you can do it all together at the same time. Otherwise, it'll take a lot of luck, time, or gold to pay people.

Lastly, you need a source of income. You need to be able to farm gold or materials that you can sell for gold on the AH. This will get turned into raid consumes and is going to be a large factor in if any raid groups let you tag along. Some are very accommodating to people who come prepared, so finding a slot will probably be easier than you expect (Natare is a great place to start imo), but if you want to do so repeatedly you'll need to ensure you're not a burden on the team. This doesn't mean absolutely maxed-out everything-possible pre-raid (skullflame shield is too expensive man), but it does mean showing initiative with some enchants, solid gear, and all of your consumes. It's a plus to review the fights beforehand and I've only met two raid teams that don't like it when you ask questions, but they don't take PuGs anyways so no loss there.

That's all I can think of off the top of my head. Good luck.

subject: Re: How do you Raid?
content_md:
1. Discord channels can give prebis list, even after class changes.
But honestly, for entry raids it is not expected. Only hunt preBIS if you feel like it.
The rule I usually follow (unless we're talking about tanking): for entry-level raids, have at least blue and at least lvl 50 items at each item slot.
I saw people mocking a player who joined Kara 10 PUG with lvl 40 greens and that was kinda justified.

 2. It's more complicated. To be a core member of a guild, regular attendance is expected. But being a core usually just means that there are certain items only they can SR. Unless the guild is really big and core means an A team, but then, they usually have a B team, too.
You can easily join a guild and raid let's say once in a month, if you accept that the best items will be probably locked from you.

PUG is another option. There are usually some HRs but you can easily join some and gear up.
Just ask around and notice if a PUG is 1. a scam (half the stuff is on HR) 2. toxic (certain people or guilds can be kinda verbally abusive, I'd avoid such PUGs).
But decent PUGs are prime way to gear up.

Kara10, AQ20, ZG, MC, Ony are the entry-level raids. PUG-ed often.
ES normal mode, BWL still kinda frequent but better gears are expected.
ES hard mode, AQ40, Naxx, Kara40 (around in that order): PUGs getting rarer and better gear is more and more expected.

You can mitigate some lack of gear with good consumes. But only overdo if you are rich in-game.
F.ex. flasking in BWL feels like rather a flex than a necessity.

author: Nikaboyoluffy
subject: Gold Reward on Raid Bosses
content_md:
I believe that it would make the raiding environment more rewarding to players who get loot and who do not a static amount of gold per boss (**10-15 gold on each boss killed**).

 **PROS:**

 1 - Encourages pick-up-group (PUG) raids to not disband.
 2 - If players' soft-reserved (SR) loot does not drop they will still remain for the gold rewards that they can use to build their wealth for gear or consume requirements (i.e. fire resist gear, elixirs, and flasks).
 3 - If the PUG is stuck on a boss mechanic the gold reward from the boss kill cover their raid / repair costs.
 4 - Encourages players who do not raid an incentive to join the community of raiders and learn the fights.
 5 - Creates a more positive learning and completion raiding environment as the entire raid will be working towards the same goal (GOLD!) if their targeted loot does not drop.
 6 - Allows guilds to build their coffers VIA boss kills too, versus just hard-reserving (HR) materials for further content progression.
 7 - Would make the players who do obtain loot feel more rewarded as they both get their gear and gold reward from raid, and a reason to stay in the raid if their loot does drop.
 8 - Longer play times from players who raid as there is an incentive to complete the entire raid for extra gold, versus just doing specific bosses for boss completion (for example Zul'Gurub).
 9 - Stabilizes player retention for players who consistently "get nothing" from raids then quit. A small, guaranteed reward helps retain raiders across dry loot streaks.
 10 - Easy to implement and scale.

 **CONS:**
 1 - Gold rewards may devalue the feeling of getting rare or powerful gear, and at the end of the day us gamers like feeling better than the other.
 2 - Classic WoW thrives on the thrill of loot drops—adding static gold makes the loot feel less impactful or special.
 3 - Encourages GDKP and RMT behavior and will put extra work on the devs to make sure that does not happen on this server.
 **4 - Classic WoW is built around scarcity, difficulty, and social organization. Adding guaranteed gold shifts the feel toward modern retail WoW design, which will alienate most of the core Classic player base.**
 5 - More gold in the server = easier access to top-tier consumables and gear = higher expectations = more pressure on raiders (new and elite) to perform at even higher levels.

I would love to hear the community / devs thoughts on a change like this, also I'd like to do a vote, but I'm not sure how. If any advice please let me know!

As an aside, it's not in interest of any WoW private server to fully cover costs of raiding by earning gold from killing bosses in the raids. Mc gives ~50g per player on a full run.
Naxx is closer to 80g

Injecting much more gold drop into the only activity endgame players spend their money on not only causes inflation, it turns one of the few goldsinks the game has into a gold generator.

If you want to give a pity reward for people who didnt get their loot, you can add a token system for some bad luck protection (aka bring me 40 of nefarians scales which drop every week as a bop for each player) and i give you a weaker tear or you use it to fund/refund their consumables. But not by giving raw gold but instead a bag with random bufffood/potions

I dont think such a system is needed. The only raids you dont make money with in most cases are naxx and kara40. And those are not places for making money by any metric

author: Afraido23
subject: Karazhan 10 is bad design and here is why
content_md:
**Lower Karazhan Halls: The Worst Raid Design in the Game**

Let’s be honest — Lower Karazhan Halls (Kara10) is arguably the worst-designed raid in the game. Here is why:

 **1. The Difficulty — or Lack Thereof**

Kara10 is the textbook definition of a "tank and spank" raid. There’s virtually no risk of wiping due to complex mechanics or lacking DPS. While some players consider it a chill, laid-back raid, the reality is that it's mind-numbingly dull. You can switch off your brain, spam your basic rotation, and still clear it with ease. The only variable that affects clear time is your group’s gear level. Honestly, UBRS presents more of a challenge than Kara10.

 **2. Uninspired Mechanics and Environment**

The raid’s mechanics are as bland as they come:
- The first boss just spawns adds.

- The worgen boss requires a simple tank taunt rotation or a Paladin bubble.

- The imp boss does some generic fire AoE.

- The spider boss spits poison and spawns eggs no one cares about.

- Moroes? Just another OT requirement.
That’s it. Nothing creative, nothing engaging. The environment is no better — a linear tower filled with trash mobs. There's no optional content, no profession interactions, and nothing unique you can do as a particular class. You can’t Mind Control, Enslave, or Tame anything interesting. There are no summonable secret bosses, class-specific interactions, or meaningful choices. About the only thing worth mentioning is that you can drink some booze off the floor. That’s the highlight.

 **3. The Loot — Hilariously Imbalanced**

Now for the real kicker: the loot. For the most part, Kara10’s loot is utterly forgettable — except for one item. The Scythe of Elune.

This isn’t just a good item. It’s the best item in the entire game — and it drops from the easiest raid, with a 2% drop rate, purely based on RNG. Who thought this was a good idea?

This design is baffling. The most powerful, build-defining legendary in the game is locked behind a mindless raid and random chance. It goes against the entire spirit of earning your rewards through difficult content. It’s demoralizing to see someone decked out in greens and blues suddenly obtain the best item in the game because the dice rolled in their favor.

And it gets worse — only certain classes (casters) benefit from the Scythe, so they’re the only ones interested in running Kara10. That creates a funnel effect where the raid becomes nothing more than a farming ground for a handful of players, while everyone else has no reason to care.

Imagine if Turtle randomly added a 1% drop chance BiS legendary bow for Hunters in AQ20 — Hunters would flood the raid endlessly while everyone else would avoid it. The frustration would be universal and justified. That kind of loot design just shouldn’t exist.

 **In summary:** Lower Karazhan Halls isn’t just a badly designed raid — it’s a masterclass in how not to create content. It's boring to play, forgettable in design, and completely broken in reward structure. If Turtle wanted to create the perfect storm of wasted potential, Kara10 is it. A trash raid with a jackpot prize — and that’s not clever, it’s just lazy.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Karazhan 10 is bad design and here is why
content_md:
It's an entry-level raid. The mechanics are perfectly fine. It's a great raid to teach new players about pulls, switching to adds, not standing in fire, doing taunt rotations, prioritizing certain trashmobs over others, doing skips, positioning, etc.

It's easily accessible and a breeze to run through. It has great early-raid gear for many classes. Merlot is a desired consumable. Semi-rare recipes drop. There's quite a bit of incentive to keep running it even if your gear is better, and even more now that T3.5 needs Overcharged Ley Energies to turn in.

I think it's one of the better designs as it perfectly hits the spot between UBRS and MC. Nothing more, nothing less.

You seem more salty about the Scythe than the raid? It gets easier if you stop feeling like you're entitled to it. Yes, the design behind acquiring Scythe is horrid and the powerlevel is way overtuned, but it's a legendary. It's bonus, not something every caster should run around with. Imo they should have never increased the drop rate.
But if you're in a guild that kills Mephistroth - just set up farms for just the first boss. Atiesh-port there after a big raid, you'll be done in 10 minutes. Legendaries are group efforts and this is one of the easiest to farm.

"It's an entry-level raid."
I half-agree. Loot quality tips it over harder ones, though.

"1. The Difficulty — or Lack Thereof"
I somewhat disagree.
Some parts are indeed very easy but there are more complex parts.
Eg:
The werewolf boss with stacks.
Imp rooms.
Servants' aoe silence can be messy and force caster to position correctly, specially near the end.
Those skellies spamming arcane aoe can be nasty.

But I agree that some parts are meh.
First boss is tank and spank with summons.
Spider boss seems interesting but a shaman basically kills the whole poison mechanic. Only to-do is to smash eggs.
Moroes is really underwhelming.

"2. Uninspired Mechanics and Environment"
I mostly answered this earlier.
Outside the stacking werewolf and the Grizikil, I agree.
Summoner boss should summon either more mobs or nastier mobs.
Spider should use mass poison, disease and curse (maybe even magic) to make it more interesting than poison cleansing totem goes brr.
Moroes... Well it should be improved in many ways rn.

"3. The Loot — Hilariously Imbalanced"
I disagree here. Scythe is here because Kara10 is thematically linked to Kara40.
The other loots are really strong for an entry.level raid (arguably too pushed) but atm server is so overgeared people just forget that loots below T2,5 at least were once considered cool.

The blue tanking trinket with a bunch of stam and armor. Bears love it.
Really good healing pants.
Cool melee cloak.
Extremely good melee plate head.
Legacy.

My main problem with the raid is that based on raid size and somewhat difficulty, it feels like an introductory raid, almost an UBRS with ID.
But loot-wise it jumps ZG and AQ20. Would almost consider MC too but it has some really broken items.

content_md:
I think what makes Kara10 easy raid is lack of risk of pulling too many mobs. For example UBRS despite being short dungeon has many, many places where someone could aggro packs.

First rooms where Orcish Warlocks are - they can flee and pull another room usually . Egg room - if you fall from the first floor you can wipe whole group. Mobs on the floor can kick players so it's not easy. And this room full of packs where you must kill each pack one by one.

UBRS itself is very easy if you ignore this fact. Meanwhile Kara10 has no spots to be careful at. Maybe there is one spot where people usually jump to have shorter way to Moroes - if someone pulls aggro, mobs will go via longer way and pull other packs. But it's rather skill issue if you pull them. And I think this is the reason why Kara10 seems to be so easy.

I dunno what OP is smoking about loot being trash in Kara10, stuff here is above ZG and up there with MC / Ony / Pre-BWL loot.. many groups I've been with, I saw people SR all kinds of items from every boss, even the spider aside from bear tank trinket, it has a nice blue caster pieces. content_html:
Lower Karazhan Halls: The Worst Raid Design in the Game

Let’s be honest — Lower Karazhan Halls (Kara10) is arguably the worst-designed raid in the game. Here is why:

1. The Difficulty — or Lack Thereof

Kara10 is the textbook definition of a "tank and spank" raid. There’s virtually no risk of wiping due to complex mechanics or lacking DPS. While some players consider it a chill, laid-back raid, the reality is that it's mind-numbingly dull. You can switch off your brain, spam your basic rotation, and still clear it with ease. The only variable that affects clear time is your group’s gear level. Honestly, UBRS presents more of a challenge than Kara10.

2. Uninspired Mechanics and Environment

The raid’s mechanics are as bland as they come:
  • The first boss just spawns adds.
  • The worgen boss requires a simple tank taunt rotation or a Paladin bubble.
  • The imp boss does some generic fire AoE.
  • The spider boss spits poison and spawns eggs no one cares about.
  • Moroes? Just another OT requirement.
That’s it. Nothing creative, nothing engaging. The environment is no better — a linear tower filled with trash mobs. There's no optional content, no profession interactions, and nothing unique you can do as a particular class. You can’t Mind Control, Enslave, or Tame anything interesting. There are no summonable secret bosses, class-specific interactions, or meaningful choices. About the only thing worth mentioning is that you can drink some booze off the floor. That’s the highlight.

3. The Loot — Hilariously Imbalanced

Now for the real kicker: the loot. For the most part, Kara10’s loot is utterly forgettable — except for one item. The Scythe of Elune.

This isn’t just a good item. It’s the best item in the entire game — and it drops from the easiest raid, with a 2% drop rate, purely based on RNG. Who thought this was a good idea?

This design is baffling. The most powerful, build-defining legendary in the game is locked behind a mindless raid and random chance. It goes against the entire spirit of earning your rewards through difficult content. It’s demoralizing to see someone decked out in greens and blues suddenly obtain the best item in the game because the dice rolled in their favor.

And it gets worse — only certain classes (casters) benefit from the Scythe, so they’re the only ones interested in running Kara10. That creates a funnel effect where the raid becomes nothing more than a farming ground for a handful of players, while everyone else has no reason to care.

Imagine if Turtle randomly added a 1% drop chance BiS legendary bow for Hunters in AQ20 — Hunters would flood the raid endlessly while everyone else would avoid it. The frustration would be universal and justified. That kind of loot design just shouldn’t exist.


In summary: Lower Karazhan Halls isn’t just a badly designed raid — it’s a masterclass in how not to create content. It's boring to play, forgettable in design, and completely broken in reward structure. If Turtle wanted to create the perfect storm of wasted potential, Kara10 is it. A trash raid with a jackpot prize — and that’s not clever, it’s just lazy.

My only criticism about Kara 10 is that there are too many imps to kill. It gets repetitive and tedious quickly, making the dungeon feel more like a chore than an adventure.

Also, the dungeon lacks a truly iconic mechanic. Right now, it’s mostly just narrow corridors packed with mobs. There’s nothing that really makes the place stand out or feel unique.

I think this dungeon has the perfect atmosphere to introduce something more creative — like parkour elements, such as floating platforms or environmental challenges. It would make players engage with the dungeon itself, not just the NPCs inside.

But beyond that, here are a couple more ideas:
  • Nemesis Mechanic: After defeating a certain boss, a powerful ghostly entity (a "Nemesis") is unleashed. It’s immortal, moves very slowly, and has a short-range aura that deals lethal damage if you stay too close for too long. Players would have to keep moving and stay aware of its presence while clearing the rest of the dungeon. It would add tension and a sense of being hunted in a haunted place.
  • Magical Instability: At random intervals, the dungeon experiences surges or suppressions of magical energy. Different schools of magic (Fire, Arcane, Shadow, etc.) could become temporarily stronger or weaker, affecting both players and enemy spellcasters. It would force players to adapt their strategies on the fly and reinforce the arcane chaos within Karazhan.
Of course, some players might not love things like parkour or unpredictable mechanics, but even one of these ideas could give Kara 10 a stronger identity and more replay value. Right now, it just needs something to elevate it beyond mob-clearing.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Raid progression order
content_md:
UBRS < K10/ZG < MC/Ony < AQ20/ES NM < BWL < ES HM < AQ40 < Naxx < K40

If you want "tiers", from the perspective of Nordanaar (the main server):
Full world-chat PUG tier: UBRS, K10, ZG, MC, Ony, AQ20, ES NM
Needs core but can easily take randos with them: BWL, ES HM
Actual raids for stable cores: AQ40, Naxx
A challenge not everyone will beat: K40

Nordanaar is a very old, very progressed server. The last round of Class Changes in November 2024 have also put raid damage into overdrive and in two days it'll probably go up again. So, "progression" is mostly an empty husk right now. People jump into ES and BWL on fresh 60 characters, hitching a ride with a progressed guild. Even on a new guild it doesn't take months, it takes weeks. But MC is set to receive an overhaul in 2 days, that might shake things up, who knows.

subject: Golemagg core hound mechanics ?!?!

Is anyone able to explain the mechanics of the ads on the Golemagg fight?

Half the fight they don't do anything, everything's fine.
Then one second they suddenly have 10k threat on a mage and they drop all other threat.
Another second they completely threat reset to 0.
Then right away they get 10 threat on a warlock.

I am trying to figure out what they're actually doing because it sure as hell doesn't look like one tank is able to hold one ad with their abilities.

it's like somebody vibecoded threat reset.

Problem is, if the raid mechanics are so random and not in line with the players' abilities, then there's no game to be played.

Also the slow debuff - unable to be countered by Hand of Freedom - another shitty mechanic, because if I can't use my abilities to react to the abilities of the enemies, then why do I even have abilities in the first place...

author: Zmarotrix
subject: Let's Discuss the Molten Core Rework & The Soul of Vanilla WoW
content_md:
**Hello everyone,**

I'm starting this discussion because I believe the recent changes to Molten Core touch on something deeper than just boss mechanics—they touch on the very identity of this server and its commitment to the "vanilla feel." I want to share my thoughts, not just as a raider, but as someone who deeply values the design philosophy that made this game a classic.

To be clear, my perspective is rooted in the vanilla experience. Balance should be considered from the point of view of a guild in pre-raid blues, and custom features like Dual Specialization shouldn't be a prerequisite for clearing the game's first-ever raid.

---
 **The Unseen Pillar of Vanilla: The Feeling of Progression**
Before diving into specific bosses, we need to talk about *why* Molten Core matters so much. In Vanilla, progression isn't just about loot; it's a carefully crafted journey. Molten Core is the first step. It’s designed to be simple, to teach 20-40 people how to coordinate, how to learn the basics of threat, positioning, and endurance. From there, BWL adds complexity, AQ40 adds chaos, and Naxx demands mastery.

Molten Core *should* be clearable by a dedicated group in dungeon blues. If that foundation is broken, the entire progression ladder of the game is severed at its root.

This leads to a more profound, emotional pillar of the game—the reward for that progression. I think this is the most important part of the entire discussion:

> **My Core Belief wrote:**
> One of the most defining features of Vanilla World of Warcraft is its ability to make you truly feel like you are getting stronger. Returning to these older raids you once struggled to clear just to obliterate them feels unbelievably rewarding. It's one of the primary draws of Vanilla World of Warcraft and it's incredibly important for preserving the vanilla feel of the game.

This feeling isn't just a minor feature; it's woven into the very fabric of Vanilla's identity. It's the silent reward for your effort. When we alter that fundamental journey, the change might not feel jarring in the moment, but it subtly erodes the long-term memories and experiences that draw us to this game. The view from the mountaintop is less breathtaking if the path up the first hill is a sheer cliff face.

---
 **What's Good: A Tip of the Hat**
The new wing, new bosses, and the loot they provide are fantastic additions. They successfully address gearing gaps created by Turtle's unique class and spec changes and add fresh content, which is always welcome. The problem isn't the new content, but the revision of the old.

---
 **Where The Rework Deviates From The Path**
While some bosses feel fine, several key encounters have been changed in ways that feel contrary to Molten Core’s original design philosophy.
---
 **Magmadar**

The issue here isn’t just increased difficulty, but a change in the nature of the fight. By spawning so many pools of fire over a much longer fight, the encounter becomes a slow burn of attrition. Healers run out of mana and the room fills with fire, not because of a mistake, but simply because the fight is tuned to last that long. It's a test of endurance that feels more appropriate for a later raid tier.
---
 **Garr**

While the reduced initial damage on the pull is a great quality-of-life change, the new damage reduction mechanic feels like bloat. Garr was already one of the most strategically challenging fights in the instance, requiring coordination and precise execution. Adding more layers here doesn't feel necessary and overcomplicates an already effective encounter.
---
 **Baron Geddon**

Let's call this what it is: this is the Season of Discovery mechanic. It makes an already punishing mechanic even more so without adding creative depth. Baron’s purpose was to be a simple, brutal lesson: "manage this debuff or you will wipe your raid." The new fire patches don't enhance that lesson; they just add another layer of punishment.
---
 **Golemagg**

This is, by far, the most destructive change to the raid's structure. The Core Hounds' new fixate mechanic, combined with the longer fight duration that now necessitates a tank swap on the boss, creates an absurd tanking requirement of at least 6 tanks. In a 20-person raid, this means nearly a third of your raid force is dedicated to tanking. The resulting loss of DPS is catastrophic, not just for this fight, but for the entire instance. With other bosses having increased health pools, that DPS is not a luxury—it's a necessity. This single encounter's change fundamentally breaks the raid's composition and jeopardizes the viability of the entire run. It's a requirement that belongs in Naxxramas, not Molten Core.
---
 **Majordomo Executus**

The original Majordomo encounter was far from simple; it was a masterclass in strategic complexity. It was a tightly choreographed dance requiring perfect CC assignments, precise positioning, and flawless execution from every single player. The challenge was not in complex mechanics, but in perfect coordination. Buffing health pools and adding more disruptive teleports doesn't enhance this intricate strategic puzzle. Instead, it just layers raw punishment on top of an already demanding encounter, making it needlessly harder without adding any meaningful depth. The fight's original strategic elegance has been muddied.

---
 **A Warning: The Pandora's Box of Rewriting Vanilla**
Let me be absolutely clear: this is not a post against change. New content, new quests, and new zones are what make Turtle WoW special. I applaud those efforts.

But there is a world of difference between **adding** to the world and **rewriting** its history.

The Molten Core rework is, in my opinion, the single biggest deviation from the vanilla spirit this server has ever made. This isn't "Vanilla+." Adding a new dungeon is Vanilla+. This is different. This is going back and fundamentally changing the original, core experience. It alters the foundational identity of the game we came here to play.

This sets a dangerous precedent. It opens a Pandora's Box that, once opened, is very difficult to close. It asks a very serious question about the future of this server: Are we preserving a classic experience while adding to its world, or are we beginning to create a custom re-imagining?

Both are valid paths for a server to take, but we must be honest about which one we are on, and what that means for the soul of the game.

Thank you for reading, and I genuinely want to hear what you all think.

subject: Re: Let's Discuss the Molten Core Rework & The Soul of Vanilla WoW
content_md: Great post and I agree that this feels like a big shift in the identity of the server. Feels less like Vanilla+ and more like a total rework. My guess is the original retuning was just going to be a simple +20% boss HP so the fights aren't over in seconds, then the end of SoD and the hype for the other pserver pushed the devs to overtune in the hopes of capturing the "Classic Remastered" playerbase that desires more of a struggle at the endgame. author: Zvyrhol
subject: Re: Let's Discuss the Molten Core Rework & The Soul of Vanilla WoW
content_md:
It's hard to disagree with you, very good post. Molten Core has been known as the first big raid in World of Warcraft history. During Vanilla timeline it was indeed known as an instance where you begin your raiding journey. Thus, the raid should retain it's original simplicity because it was (at least I think so) designed as a beginner's raid.

You pointed out some new mechanics that stand against design philosophy of the first raid. MC was to teach you the basics: if you get debuff, go away or otherwise you blow up the raid. Your friends got debuff? Maybe you should dispel/decurse them? You stand in fire? Maybe you should move away?

Bosses have been revamped so now as a beginner you should control more things. It would be generally ok if it was done to raids like BWL or AQ40 that require more raiding experience. But keep in mind this is opening-raid for new raiders! Mechanics can't be too complex because otherwise newcomers might overwhelmed and quit the game!

However, I understand the reason devs decided to do so. They complained that geared players treated MC as a farm raid that is finished within 30 minutes (not many guilds are that good btw). So instead of fixing the reason why geared players farmed this raid (legendary items, powerful loot), they lifted up the level of difficulty so the geared players could spend more time here. The effect is that newcomers suffer because the raid is too hard.

content_md:
for the updates, I agree with things like bringing back Ragnaros's submerge, buffing up Lucifron a bit, these are problems like the one Anub'Rekhan has where the locusts can't come out throughout his whole fight.. But the Golemagg and Majordomo stuff I'm not too sure about..
His dogs mechanics seem way too extra for an introductory raid and it just, genuinely feels very wrong as far as game design goes, because those 2 dogs weren't supposed to be anymore of a threat than, 2 tanks and healers on those tanks, hold them for the whole duration of the fight, while the MT and another tank took care of Golemagg's stacks.

Then you have Majordomo, who was just the right amount of hard for the kind of fight it was and one of the best examples of using different comps. This fight had more than enough complicated stuff to juggle for any kind of raid, as well as enough damage to keep everyone awake and I don't remember an MC pug where I snoozed through this fight, we've always had 2 mages taking care of 2 Healers, 1-2 hunters kiting 2 Elites and tanks being assigned their targets, whether it's 1 or 2 elites at a time, as well as Executus himself.

I just ask, is that seriously not good enough for the penultimate boss of MC? because Majordomo even before buffs, was still a far more complicated fight than any of the new additions we've seen in the Old Shadowforge side.

for me this is more of a holistic view on the difficulty and gear progression throughout the raiding content of Vanilla.. Where the hell do you want Molten Core to be? Is it the First 40 man raid, or not? Make up your minds about that, Don't just make MC as hard as other raids, while keeping its loot just as dismal as it's always been.

author: Manletow
subject: 40 man Raids are inherently terrible
content_md:
In my opinion of course. ![😊](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f60a.svg)

PVE (especially 40 man Raids) shoehorn you into dedicated roles resulting in boring, static gameplay
typically spamming 1 or 2 buttons over and over

> ironic & tragic twist: this simplistic basic bitch gameplay is then lavishly rewarded with the most insanely broken and overpowered items/gear in the game

T-WoW devs are obviously very much aware of this lame gameplay which is why they keep implementing new custom abilities to "spice it up"

the problem?

every (significant) change has had disastrous consequences for PVP health & balance
(and sometimes the balance of other things -- such as faction balance)

just a small handful of examples:
Mage is broken for a whole variety of reasons (mostly custom crap)
Rogues autoattacks melting Tanks (and everyone) with Holy Strike Poison (AKA dissolvant)
 10k hp Bear Druids self-healing their entire HP Bars with 'Frenzied Regen"
Most infamously: Paladins had a 3 year period wherein they were allowed to 1-shot players with Holy Strike.

^these changes were all specifically intended to make Raiding an enjoyable experience

my point is that you simply cannot make Raids enjoyable becuz they are fundamentally broken/bad
if you attempt to fix them -- it breaks the other 50% of the game (PVP)

My suggestion:
Stop trying to make Raids Good
its ruining my PVP.

Thank you for your consideration in this matter. ![😊](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f60a.svg)

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Raids are inherently terrible content
content_md:
I want to add that raids ruin pve too.
Instead of using all class abilities, people optimise their classes to 1 button specs with only measurable metric, which is DPS.
In 5 ppl content every DPS can also use his CC abilities to help party to clear content with less resources. How often mages sheep targets in MC? Like once? How often they could do that in Deadmines? Like in every single pack.

Instead of varied experience depending on party composition, your raid follow the same scenario every time.

Raids are also cancerous in terms of healthy gameplay. To make 40 ppl raid happen every week in static company, everyone have to obey calendar schedule. Otherwise, space and time problem can't be solved.

For some reason, people also think that tank is supposed to hold threat of ALL mobs, including slowable weaklings which are a job of mages/warlocks. This is why Concecration was made baseline for prot pallies and all other tanks have to obey to this always-aoe meta.
It is not a surprise that modern games are often designed for group of 4 people and without a tanks at all

So I agree - stop trying to make raids good. More 5ppl content and better gear progression in pvp is the way to go.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Raids are inherently terrible content
content_md:
True, PvP is a sidenote in WoW and not its main draw. That being said much more has been sacrificed on the altar of "Raidperformance" than just PvP.

Questing and Dungeons, some of the most integral aspects of the wow gameplay loop have also been made significantly worse by those changes. Because PvP is nothing more than fighting a slightly more advanced mob of said class in many cases.

Being able to oneshot people in pvp is unhealthy - and so is doing the same to questmobs. Because the game can not be fun and challenging no matter a mobs ability if he dosnt get time to use it.

PvP is a great healthcheck for balancing because if an ability is too good to have, it will ondoubtably be noticed in pvp first.

But just because its warriors melting in pvp in seconds doesnt mean rogue poison buffs in pve was a smart choice as it makes you disproportionally less likely to use the utility poisons over the dmg ones. Robbing the game of a tactical aspect

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Raids are inherently terrible content
content_md:
I often see that "pvp was a sidenote" thesis. I totally disagree with it.
PvP was supposed to be the pinnacle of character progression, not the thing that you do when bored. It was like exam to your gear/skill check.

Reasons:
 1. Literally half of abilities that exist in the game are used only for pvp. Disarm, silence, spell interrupts, manaburn, slow and anti-slow abilities.
 2. Blizzard was a company which made Warcraft 3 - highly competitive game with tournaments and prizes. They also made Diablo 2 and get good experience in making pvp there. They know how to make pvp in general. They just have to solve "how to make pvp in group setting".
 3. This game was made with 2 faction from the start. It is naturally lead to fighting against eachother.

If you compare wow to any other cooperative game, you notice that wow is quite good even now. It relies too heavily on tank+healer+dps model, but as long as it is fun, why not?

One more thing about raids being bad. They bend economy of the server to consumable farming. Half of the problem with economics comes from the fact that people have to drink all possible elixirs each raid. Instead of gimmik that boosted people a bit, it become mandatory tax for every man involved.
If you do pvp all the time, you won't get enough time to gather consumables.

author: Annoying
subject: Re: Raids are inherently terrible content
content_md:
The problem with all these later raids is that they make the gear too powerful (with much higher item level) compared to what a somewhat fresh 60 is wearing.

Nothing wrong with adding pve content in general, but don't keep adding more and more powerful items.

A lvl 60 epic should not be that much better than a lvl 58 epic for example (in terms of stats).
Like there are no way better low level epics of the same level in the game in terms of much higher item level.

Back in the day there were a lot of casuals playing.
Most people that played on my server were running around with quest/dungeon gear, some had perhaps a few pieces from MC, BWL or rank gear (blue), they did just fine in pvp.

Today you really can't join with some quest/dungeon blues and expect to have a good time in battlegrounds or in pvp in general.

Another problem is that twinks can get too powerful (especially at lvl 19 and lvl 29) with all the lvl 60 enchants they can use and high stat gear (fishing or grand arena trinket for example) that for some reason don't have a level restriction.

It ruins pvp for the new guy as they have no chance in hell vs twinks with again regular quest and dungeon gear.

Another contribution to the pvp mess is all the recent class changes and in my opinion, the ridiculous changes to the pvp trinket dumbing down the game.
And just overpowered gear in general.

I used to focus on lvl 49 twinking as I thought it was the most balanced and fair in pvp.

But rogues and druids with proc on hit gear combined with Blade of Eternal Darkness is just too broken.

I have one myself, but its just not fun to only smash one button knowing that you do more dps than they and that they can't get a heal or spell off because of all the pushback from all the gear procs.

Besides, Blizzard were already working on TBC in 2004 (officially being announced on October 28, 2005) so I doubt they had balance (of all aspects of the game) at 60 forever in mind when creating raids like Naxx in vanilla as you were eventually going to level to lvl 70 anyways.

I asked AI: How many players used aq40/naxx gear in the original world of warcraft?

AI:
> It's difficult to determine an exact number, but only a small percentage of Original WoW players used full AQ40/Naxx gear, with estimates suggesting only about 1% of the player base reached Naxxramas. This was due to the difficulty of the raids, the long grind required, and the high player attrition rate for that phase of the game, where many players quit before reaching endgame content.
>
>  Limited Access: Raids like AQ40 and Naxxramas were extremely difficult, with many guilds struggling to progress or even enter.
>
>  High Attrition: The player base often dwindled significantly by the time these raids were current content, with many players quitting before they could reach this point in the game.
>
>  Small Percentage: Sources suggest that a tiny fraction, potentially around 1%, of the total player base ever saw Naxxramas, let alone cleared it and acquired full gear.
>
>  Server-Specific Variation: The number of players with this gear was higher on some servers than others. On very populated servers, a few guilds might have been "farming" AQ40 and Naxxramas, but this was not the norm.
>
>  No Official Data: Blizzard does not release official numbers, so any figures are based on community estimates, forum discussions, and historical data from fan sites and Reddit.

You know, this matter actually very complex.
You are right by every point, but it is not "absolute truth". Everything is true, but for different types of players and in different proportions.

First thing that I am totally sure is that pvp is harder than pve. Instead of being guarded by tank and healed by heal, you have to overcome incoming damage and CC.
This alone might be a good reason for large portion of players not to involve at all.

As a consequence of this, it is normal that people do PvE first and only then go to PvP.
It is true for battlegrounds now. Large portion of players come into raids (or dungeons on lower levels), get bis or pre-bis gear and then go pvp. Even if we disable OP enchants, world buffs and stuff like AGM/furbolg medicine pouch, there are different players in term of power. Some are equipped in BiSes and enchant leather armor kits to their gear. Others are either passers-by or dedicated pvp players who know that to do if you are undergeared.

It raises the question. Why people should go PvP, if they already geared?
 1. Some go to stomp less prepared players.
 2. Stopped xp sub-twinks. They go to test own skill and progress and to overcome difficulties.
 3. Levelers. When turtle allowed xp from bgs, they have more reasons to queue.
Who will play longer? My bet is - 2nd and 3rd groups players. You don't need to play for long time to feel good.
Do we need to encourage first group to play more? I doubt so. They naturally join for 1 or 2 matches. They have obvious advantage which explains why they are winning. They are not interested in progress.
But this group of players need others - the ones to kill - 2nd and 3rd group of playres.
 2nd and 3rd group of players need some reason to join even if they lose.
Now battlegrounds only encourage winning. Wins provide highest progress.
How to encourage 2nd group of players? By setting long term goal. Most of people go 10-19 for exalted xp in wsg. Then they going to graduate to 20 and grind exalted in arathi. This group is not interested in xp, because they stopped it. Reputational items should be a bit better than PvE ones. Like 1-2 points of stats is enough. It just just look better to be worth grinding, but doesn't have to be overwhelmengly better.
Scout Medallion is good example. 6 agi+2sta while there are other 2 stamina necks from JC now.
Outrunner bow is questionable example. +3 damage compared to Venomstrike, but don't have proc on shot.
How to encourage 3rd group of players? Just give them xp equal to their time spent. Even when they see ghosthealer, they should know that they got some cheap progress. Give xp for grabbing/returning flag or for picking restoration boost or for carrying flag to some special place (like exit of ramp or tonnel). I think they can even get full xp from losing match. It is not big deal actually. Xp is free. But those players will provide enough "meat" for others.

So losses should grant experience. It is exactly like it was with old Warmode (20/30% to xp from killing mobs), but with three major differences:
a. You explicitly queue to fight and you make this decision every time. Warmode challenge was opt-in at the start and opt out twice. You can queue bg as much as you can. You don't have to queue bg
b. It is not mixed with PvE - you get xp only from pvp objectives.
c. there is no bluewalling in battlegrounds. You can't get Ambush or Pyroblast from unflagged player.

content_html:
I often see that "pvp was a sidenote" thesis. I totally disagree with it.
PvP was supposed to be the pinnacle of character progression, not the thing that you do when bored. It was like exam to your gear/skill check.

Reasons:
1. Literally half of abilities that exist in the game are used only for pvp. Disarm, silence, spell interrupts, manaburn, slow and anti-slow abilities.
2. Blizzard was a company which made Warcraft 3 - highly competitive game with tournaments and prizes. They also made Diablo 2 and get good experience in making pvp there. They know how to make pvp in general. They just have to solve "how to make pvp in group setting".
3. This game was made with 2 faction from the start. It is naturally lead to fighting against eachother.


If you compare wow to any other cooperative game, you notice that wow is quite good even now. It relies too heavily on tank+healer+dps model, but as long as it is fun, why not?

One more thing about raids being bad. They bend economy of the server to consumable farming. Half of the problem with economics comes from the fact that people have to drink all possible elixirs each raid. Instead of gimmik that boosted people a bit, it become mandatory tax for every man involved.
If you do pvp all the time, you won't get enough time to gather consumables.
"PvP was supossed to be the pinacle of Character Progression"
-WoW started without PvP.

author: Elesion
subject: On Farm Raids (and why they should not be changed)
content_md:
**The Concept of Farm Raids**
There is a time period in gameplay where you tackle new challenges. You discover a new instance, you develop new strategies, you put your time and effort into the exhausting task of beating an actual challenge. That time period is called "progression" and usually lasts a few weeks.
After progression you enter the "optimization" phase, where you polish your strategies so they become solid and repeatable. Everything should be stable and reliable. This is not very fun, but quite rewarding as your clear-times improve. That can take some weeks to a few months.
And lastly you enter the final phase of the raid lifecycle - "farm". That phase is of infinite length (especially on a forever-Vanilla server like TWoW). Nothing new happens, you just repeat the same ol' week after week.

 **The Draw of Farm Raids**
If it's that rote, why do people continue to run farm raids?
1. To get rare items. Vanilla is a game of grinds. With how scarce and RNG-heavy loot is, it's routine that people wait many months to win particular items.
2. To enjoy brain-less gameplay. There's an entire genre of games where you grind repetitive tasks (something like a Stardew Valley) and people love them. And it's actually pretty sweet if an entire raid team enters a "flow" state and the raid runs itself on muscle memory without a raid leader having to give directions.
3. To sozialize. When you don't have to focus on the gameplay, you can focus on the people.
4. To bask in nostalgia. Can be general nostalgia for a 20yo game, or particular nostalgia for past achievements with your raid group.
5. To help out other people in your group.
6. To train and gear new people. Raid groups need fresh blood. Nothing better to give people their first important assignments than a raid where very little can go wrong.
 **Why it's a Bad Idea to change them**
Take note that "discovering new things", "having to learn new skills", or "being challenged with hard encounters" is not among the draws of a farm raid. Because that's what progression is about. You don't sign up to MC to be surprised. You sign up for MC because it's a breezy optimized clear and you want to enjoy the company of people and help the guild.
Farm raids are not grand adventures where people are sad because of the boredom after a while. Farm raids are entries on a weekly schedule, something that "has to be done" to keep the raider pipeline in your guild going. Geared and experienced people largely join to help out. They've long concluded their progression phase, long filled their need for items, and moved their focus onto higher tiers.

So if you make the experience unpleasant - by overtuned requirements, by needlessly introducing new mechanics, by drastically altering established routing - there might be a few people who enjoy the novelty. But by and large you spread misery to and steal time from the thousands of players who run those instances as farm raids. Their weekly schedule just got longer for no appreciable reward. Raids are less approachable for weaker or newer players and cannot serve as training grounds anymore. The established familiarity is disrupted. The nostalgia is disturbed. The years of muscle memory and flow state are broken.
And suddenly the former farm raid has now become a chore. All the effort of progression and optimization with no pay-off, because you've been through it already. And people who previously joined to help out will think twice about turning up because of the annoyance and additional time commitment. And guess what happens when the geared veterans lose interest? The raid becomes even slower and even more annoying to run.

Yes, MC and BWL are stale. But that's their point at this time in the server's lifecycle. They're farm raids. They're somewhere between nostalgic comfort food and weekly basic routine to keep up the pipeline from fresh 60 into the endgame. They don't need an overhaul. You can tune their numbers carefully (to compensate for class change powercreep), but please don't add or remove bosses or mechanics.
Direct your effort towards new content. TWoW is Vanilla+. Keep the Vanilla content unchanged, add the + on top. I enjoy the new content and I think a smaller MC spin-off raid would have been a lot more well-received than what has been done to beloved Molten Core with 1.18 (and what might be done to BWL and Onyxia with the next patch).

Related post from someone else: [Let's Discuss the Molten Core Rework & The Soul of Vanilla WoW](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=158970) - Molten Core was iconic and it's supposed to be easy.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: On Farm Raids (and why they should not be changed)
content_md:
The problem is not the difficulty. I even called for slight numbers adjustments to compensate for powercreep myself.
The problem is that it was changed without need, making it longer and more annoying when the vast majority of players was not looking for MC to become longer or more annoying. The fact that it was changed at all should require justification on a Vanilla-based server, regardless of the tuning question. And I don't see a good reason for it when they could have made Old Shadowforge a separate raid while leaving MC untouched.

The role that MC fills on the weekly raid schedule is not to be "slightly less boring". It's to be fully boring while you breeze through it for the third year without having to explain fight mechanics because you have it on muscle-memory-tier farm.

> **Terrydavis wrote: Sun Nov 16, 2025 11:38 pm**

I can tell you're not very deeply involved in managing a guild. Most guilds need to run lower raids to gear up new hires, train and observe them, back-fill certain super-rare items for core members, etc. And since there's only so many hours in the week you basically rely on geared core members to show up to lower raids to speed them up and make them go smooth. The changes are exactly "fine", but I liked the old version much better.
And again, having people kinda like the changes is still far away from "they were damned if they didn't make these changes", painting it as a no-win situation.
topic_title: On Farm Raids (and why they should not be changed)

subject: What piece or pieces of loot elude you, or took the longest to get?
content_md:

The two pieces of loot which have not dropped for me yet are: Wild Growth Spaulders from Barron Geddon in MC, which has only dropped once since I hit 60 in December '25 for a period approaching 3 months. So, what's the longest you've waited for a raid drop, and what item is it?

author: Auralys
subject: Balance Druid performance and gameplay issues in raids
content_md:
Hello,
After playing Balance in K40-level raids, I wanted to share some feedback on how the spec currently performs in PvE.
Right now:

DPS feels inconsistent due to heavy RNG (Eclipse procs)
Optimal play requires frequent stopcasting, which hurts fluidity and real output
No real burst or control window compared to other casters
DoTs and Hurricane not proccing trinkets significantly reduces scaling

In practice, this results in:

Lower reliability in damage output
More effort required for equal or worse results than other specs

The spec doesn’t feel competitive or rewarding in a raid setting despite proper play.

I detailed the issues and some possible improvements here:
![👉](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f449.svg) [viewtopic.php?f=42&t=24455](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?f=42&t=24455)

Would be interested to compare logs and feedback from other raiding Balance players.

author: Zarahv
subject: Adding a Tarnished Undermine Real/Badge System from other versions of WoW.
content_md:
After this latest Naxxramas run last week where I ended up yet again not receiving any loot due to poor rolls across the entire raid, I've come to the conclusion that vanilla WoW's, and Turtle's loot system by extension, is still archaic and extremely dated.

Blizzard had systems in Season of Discovery and Wrath of the Lich King Classic where you could purchase raid loot for clearing dungeons/raids to reward participation and clearing aside from simply getting lucky when a boss dies, and then even luckier by winning a dice roll against upwards of 20+ people.

Ive done over 10-11 lockouts of Naxxramas and only ended up with 2 pieces of tier 3, no other items whatsoever. I feel like earning badges/tokens for killing bosses in each wing of Naxx, or any raid for instance, should reward you with tokens for said raid where you can then spend said tokens outside of the raid for gear from corresponding bosses.

Here's a hypothetical system I've thought up, completely subject to interpretation or change by the Turtle WoW Dev Team.

Naxxramas has 15 bosses.

All loot from the 4 wings before Sapphiron/KT costs between 10 (Non-weapon)/15 (Weapon) tokens/badges to buy at a vendor at Light's Hope Chapel.

Final Boss Loot of each wing, Sapphiron and Kel'thuzad costs between 20 (Non-weapon)/30 (Weapon) tokens/badges plus a special token from each final boss so you MUST kill 20-30 bosses (2 Lockouts) +  have the respective token from each boss to purchase loot that drops from them.

That means in a minimum of a week, for your participation, you receive almost any item you desire should you put in the work and fully clear the raid. It would make going in and clearing without dreading the thought of receiving nothing completely moot, as you are guaranteed at least 1-2 items per run should you fully clear. Legendaries should not be purchasable however and still stay rare drops.

I'm willing to hear feedback if this is too easy or not, but the current slog of waiting week after week, spending thousands of gold on consumables, going into these raids and getting NOTHING heavily wanes on the psyche. I'd love to see a system like this implemented so no matter what, luck or not, gear will come to you if you put forth the effort and time to attain it.
